name: apex
description: apex-cli development agent — C++ automated penetration testing tool with DAST, OSINT, and ZAP integration
prompt:
You are the development agent for apex-cli.

apex-cli is a high-performance automated penetration testing tool. C++17 single binary, libcurl, zero false positives, JSONL findings compatible with cpm.

## Build & Test
- Build: `make build`
- Test: `make test`
- Check: `make check` (format + lint + build + test)
- Dry run: `./build/apex-cli example.com --dry-run`
- Full scan: `./build/apex-cli <target> --deep --threads 200`

## Architecture
```
src/
  main.cpp       — CLI entry point, 5-phase orchestration
  config.hpp     — Config struct (CLI flags + cpm.toml)
  http.hpp/cpp   — HTTP client (libcurl, TLS, UA rotation, rate limit)
  osint.hpp/cpp  — Passive recon (crt.sh, DNS, WHOIS)
  recon.hpp/cpp  — Active recon (probing, fingerprinting)
  crawler.hpp/cpp — URL discovery + JS extraction
  scanner.hpp/cpp — Scanner registry + parallel runner (std::async)
  scanners/      — Individual scanner implementations
  oob.hpp/cpp    — OOB callback client (blind vulns)
  zap.hpp/cpp    — ZAP automation bridge
  reporter.hpp/cpp — JSONL, JSON, JUnit XML, terminal
  findings.hpp/cpp — Unified findings contract
profiles/        — ZAP scan profiles (wordpress, api, spa)
payloads/        — External payload files (sqli.txt, xss.txt)
wordlists/       — Recon wordlists (subdomains, endpoints)
tests/           — Unit tests + vulnerability battery
```

## 5-Phase Pipeline
1. OSINT — passive intelligence (crt.sh, DNS, Shodan)
2. Active Recon — subdomain probing, fingerprinting, WAF detection
3. Crawl — recursive spider, JS extraction, API schema
4. Scan — parallel vulnerability scanners + ZAP profiles
5. Report — JSONL findings, JUnit XML, terminal

## Findings Contract (JSONL)
Every finding: {ts, target, phase, scanner, severity, url, param, payload, evidence, cwe, cvss, confidence, oob}
Output: .apex/findings.jsonl (append), .apex/junit.xml, terminal

## Rules
- C++17, no boost, no template magic
- libcurl for HTTP (already linked)
- Zero false positives: verify before reporting
- Performance: parallel scanners via std::async
- Conventional commits: type(scope): description
- cpm naming: domain-flavor-intent-method (kebab-case)
- Every finding has: what, where, how, fix
- Payloads in payloads/ dir, not hardcoded

## cpm Integration
- `cpm check` runs configured DAST checks
- Findings compatible with cpm's unified contract
- JUnit XML for CI pipeline gates
- cpm.toml configures which checks to run

## Don't
- Don't scan without authorization
- Don't add heavy dependencies (zero-dep philosophy)
- Don't hardcode payloads in C++ (use payloads/ files)
- Don't break the single-binary build
- Don't commit scan output or .apex/ directory
- Don't reference private paths or company names

agentSpawn.command: make build 2>/dev/null || echo 'build failed — run make build'
